Split DE results into up- and down-regulated genes

Source: R/process_rnaseq.R
filter_de_genes.Rd

Keeps the genes of a DE table with an adjusted p-value below `padj.cutoff` and an absolute log2 fold change above `logfc.cutoff`, split by direction.

Usage

filter_de_genes(
  data,
  logfc.cutoff = 0,
  padj.cutoff = 0.05,
  method = c("auto", "edgeR", "DESeq2", "limma", "seurat"),
  padj.col = NULL,
  logfc.col = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

data

A data frame of DE results with a log2 fold change and an adjusted p-value column (edgeR, DESeq2, limma or Seurat results, or any table with the columns given)

logfc.cutoff

Minimum absolute log2 fold change (strictly greater). Default is 0 (any change)

padj.cutoff

Maximum adjusted p-value (strictly smaller). Default is 0.05

method

The tool that produced the results: "auto" (default) detects it from the column names, as standardize_de does; or one of "edgeR", "DESeq2", "limma" and "seurat"

padj.col

Column of the (adjusted) p-values used for the ranking. If NULL (default), taken from `method` (e.g. "FDR" for edgeR, "padj" for DESeq2)

logfc.col

Column of the log2 fold changes. If NULL (default), taken from `method`

...

Deprecated names of the arguments (`de_results`, `log2fc_min`, `pvalue_max`, `de_method`, `pvalue_col`, `log2fc_col`), accepted with a warning; renamed in 0.10.0

Value

A list of two data frames, the rows of `data` that pass:

up_reg

up-regulated genes

down_reg

down-regulated genes

Examples

de <- data.frame(
    logFC = c(2.1, -1.4, 0.2), PValue = c(1e-8, 1e-4, 0.6),
    FDR = c(3e-8, 2e-4, 0.6), row.names = c("ISG15", "CD3E", "ACTB")
)
filter_de_genes(de, logfc.cutoff = 1)
#> Detected edgeR results (logFC, FDR)
#> $up_reg
#>       logFC PValue   FDR
#> ISG15   2.1  1e-08 3e-08
#> 
#> $down_reg
#>      logFC PValue   FDR
#> CD3E  -1.4  1e-04 2e-04
#>
